To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) HMM's are a natural model of information flow in sequential programs, (2) uncertainty measures are an important class of quantitative measures of information flow, and (3) the Dalenius principle is an important semantic compositionality issue for information flow.

(i) we propose to use the Giry monads to represent abstract Markov processes; (ii) we propose a new, uncertainty-transformer semantics that can be used to model the Dalenius property; (iii) we propose a novel partial ordering of abstract HMM's that can be used as a basis for a quantitative theory of information leakage.
the Giry monads are a suitable framework for representing and reasoning about HMMs, and that uncertainty measures are a suitable framework to reason about the security of information flow in HMMs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the semantic foundations for a quantitative theory of information flow in probabilistic programs.
a monadic treatment of HMM's, uncertainty measures, and Dalenius' desideratum.
the monadically abstract semantics and semantics-preserving uncertainty measures of abstract HMM's and their use as a basis for quantitative information flow analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Giry monadic account of HMM's, with the uncertainty measures as the semantic backbone, provides a framework for a monadic account of quantitative information flow in probabilistic programs.

HMM's are a monadic account of quantitative information flow, in which information flow is represented as a partial order of abstract HMM's, while information flow security is represented as an increasing function from uncertainty measures to the real numbers.
we have developed the foundations for a theory of information flow in HMM's.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have a “monadic” account of quantitative information flow in HMM's.
we propose an abstract semantics for HMMs as a monad in the Giry category and we show that it has a dual semantics based on the concept of uncertainty measure.
we have a new semantics for HMMs, and we can use this semantics to reason about the security of HMM-based probabilistic programs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the monadic type of HMM's is not X→DX but rather DX→D2DX.
monadic hiding is a more general and powerful tool for reasoning about security, than hiding over state.
monadic semantics for HMM’s, and more generally, for information flow, is a very promising direction.
